locale_code.description: The language this catalogue is written in, as a BCP-47 code. Read by the code to keep Intl.DisplayNames and plural rules on the catalogue's language - must equal the directory name.

extension_description.message: Read web articles and EPUB books offline - and learn the language you read them in. Nothing you read leaves your device.

pair_label.description: How a translation direction reads on screen. Languages whose grammar would bend the names use an arrow instead of a word.

support.description: The support section's heading on the settings page, its link in the page's table of contents, and the popup's heart row - the noun, as in backing the project.

private_browsing_note.message: You are in private browsing. Here the browser uses a separate, empty database for re/read and deletes it when the private session ends: nothing you have saved is here, and nothing you save or import here is kept. Open re/read from a normal tab - everything is there.
private_browsing_note.description: The sentence at the top of the extension's pages (reading list, reader, highlights, saved phrases, settings) when the page runs in a private window or tab: Firefox gives it a separate, in-memory database. Never shown on Chromium, whose extension pages share one database in both modes.

open_reader.message: Read this page in the reader

quiet_bubble.description: Checkbox label in the popup and on the settings page: the translation bubble opens with its buttons folded away (D81).

error_engine_missing.message: No translation engine yet - this build cannot translate.

error_model_missing.message: No model for this language pair on this device - download or add one in the settings. And to read without machine translation, switch on "Use without a translation model" there - your dictionaries still answer, and you save phrases from their meanings.

error_unsupported_pair.message: No model exists for this language pair.

error_too_long.message: That selection is too long to translate.

error_no_page.message: There is no page to read here - open an article and press the button again.

error_unknown_message.message: The extension sent a request it does not understand.

error_internal.message: Something went wrong inside the extension.

bubble_nothing_more.message: No sentence and no dictionary entry to show
bubble_nothing_more.description: The line behind the bubble's More button when the fetch it started comes back empty - shown instead of the layer closing without a word. It stands where a translated sentence normally would, so it must name the missing things (sentence, dictionary) and read unmistakably as the extension talking, never like a line of the book.

bubble_no_dictionary.message: No dictionary for $LANGUAGE$ yet - add one in the settings

bubble_speak.description: aria-label and hover title of the speaker icon in the bubble's action row (D83): speaks the selected phrase itself, never the translation.

bubble_sentence_collapse.description: aria-label and hover title of the fold in the corner of the bubble's sentence section (D96): clamps the translated sentence to one line so the dictionary entries below get the room.

bubble_sentence_expand.description: The same fold once the sentence is clamped: pressing it brings the full sentence back.

bubble_copy.description: aria-label and hover title of the copy icon in the bubble's action row (D110): opens a row with the two copy choices below.

bubble_copy_original.description: The clipboard row's first press (D110): puts the selected phrase itself - the page's own words - onto the clipboard.

bubble_copy_translation.description: The clipboard row's second press (D110): puts the translation as shown in the bubble onto the clipboard.

bubble_copied.description: Stands in for a copy press's own label for a moment after the clipboard took the text - the same feedback the reader page's highlighter bar gives.

popup_site_enabled.description: The per-site switch's label; checked means re/read runs there. $1 is the site's hostname.

popup_site_toggle_title.message: Whether re/read runs on this site

popup_no_page.message: re/read does not work on this page.

popup_no_model.message: No translation model on this device yet - press here to pick one in the settings.
popup_no_model.description: Stands in the popup where the pair select would be, while no model is stored. The whole row is a button that opens the settings page.

popup_translation_off.message: Machine translation is off - the reader and your dictionaries keep working.
popup_translation_off.description: Stands in the popup where the pair row would be while the translation-off setting (D120) is on. A plain note, not a button - since D128 the switch itself is a few rows below, so the note no longer points at the settings.

vocab_intro.message: Every phrase you kept for this language pair, newest first - saved while reading, stored only on this device. $LEARNED$ removes a phrase and its underlines with it; $EDIT$ rewrites what it means, one meaning per line.
vocab_intro.description: The buttons quoted are bubble_learned and bubble_edit, passed in so the three can never drift apart.

vocab_filter_label.message: Filter the list of saved phrases

vocab_count_filtered_one.description: The counter while the filter is active. Plural family over the total; the matching count rides along as $2.

vocab_edit_aria.description: Accessible name of a row's Edit button - a bare "Edit" in a list of a hundred names nothing.

vocab_speak_aria.description: Accessible name of a row's speaker button - it speaks the saved phrase itself, never the meanings (D83).

vocab_empty.message: Nothing is saved for this pair yet. Select a phrase while reading and press "$BUTTON$" - it will be waiting here.
vocab_empty.description: The button quoted is bubble_save, passed in so the two can never drift apart.

transfer_heading.description: Heading of the transfer section under the saved-phrases and reading lists, and the text of the anchor link that jumps to it - one name for one place.

vocab_transfer_note.message: A two-column .tsv file - what the KOReader plugin writes and Anki imports. Importing adds phrases this pair is missing and never touches a saved one.

vocab_import_nothing.message: There are no phrases to import in that file.

vocab_import_summary_one.description: Plural family over the row count; NAME is the picked file's name. The colon leads into the sample rows shown below.

vocab_import_added_one.description: First sentence of the import report, always shown. A language may bend the counted noun's case to fit its own sentence.

vocab_import_skipped_other.description: Second sentence of the import report, shown only when something was skipped.

vocab_import_unreadable_one.description: Last sentence of the import report, shown only when the file had lines that were not rows of the format.

reader_pictures_save.description: Menu row over a saved article: fetch its pictures from the article's servers and keep them with it. The count is how many the article refers to. 'Download' rather than 'Save' - it names the network act (Michał, 2026-08-29).

reader_pictures_hint.message: Downloaded once from the article's own servers, without cookies, and kept with the article on this device. After the download they are shown in the article.

reader_pictures_progress.description: The row's label while pictures are being saved; the size is what has been kept so far.

reader_pictures_done_other.description: After a download: how many of the pictures the article asked for are kept, and what they take.

reader_pictures_none.message: None of the pictures could be downloaded.

reader_pictures_failed.message: The pictures could not be written.

library_pictures_other.description: In a reading list row: the article's pictures and what they take.

reader_back_to_list.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the drawn back arrow in the reader's bar, shown while an article is on screen.

underline_fine.description: How heavily a saved phrase is underlined (D130) - the accessible name of the lightest of three swatches in the reader's Aa panel. Each swatch draws the line it stands for.

reader_speech_failed.message: This device could not read the article aloud.

reader_segment_unread_count.description: Tab label wearing the whole segment's count - the entire half of the list, not the page on screen.

reader_delete_aria.description: Accessible name of a row's Delete button - a bare "Delete" in a list of fifty names nothing.

reader_delete_confirm_aria.description: The same button, armed and asking; focus stays on it between the two presses.

reader_mark_book_read.description: A book's read mark names the whole book: over 32 parts a bare "Mark as read" left open whether the part or the book was being marked.

reader_no_article.message: There was no article to find on that page.

reader_list_write_failed.message: The reading list could not be written.

reader_empty_none.message: Nothing is saved yet - open an article in the reader and press "$BUTTON$". A saved page stays on this device and opens without a connection.
reader_empty_none.description: The button quoted is reader_save, passed in so the two can never drift apart.

reader_empty_all_read.message: Nothing left to read - everything saved is marked as read.

reader_empty_none_read.message: Nothing is marked as read yet.

reader_filter_count.description: Beside the filter while it is active: rows matching, out of the whole segment on the tab.

reader_library_note.message: Everything here is a text copy: web articles you opened in the reading view and deliberately saved, and the articles and .epub files you imported with Import below. They all open without a connection and stay on your device, even if the original page goes away.

reader_transfer_note.message: .json - a backup file holding every article saved in the re/read offline reading list, from this browser or any other browser or device where you use re/read. Import only adds the articles missing here and never overwrites one already saved. With pictures included, the backup is a .zip holding the same .json and the pictures beside it.

reader_export_pictures.description: Checkbox under the Import/Export buttons: names Export outright, so nobody reads it as an import option (Michał, 2026-08-29). Checked, the backup becomes a .zip with the pictures kept with articles.

reader_import_pictures_other.description: Second sentence of the import offer for a .zip backup: how many pictures it carries and what they take.

reader_import_pictures_added_other.description: In the import report, after the added and skipped counts.

reader_transfer_epub.description: The second line of the file-format fold on the reading list, between the .json and the export notes.

reader_transfer_books.message: Export covers articles only - books (.epub) are not exported. A book imported again has no reading position and no highlights: export the highlights on the Highlights page (.json) before deleting the book, and import that file after importing the same book again.

reader_marks_export_copy.description: Button on the page of all highlights (D168): writes reread-highlights.json, the file the Import button beside it reads back.

reader_marks_import.description: Button beside the backup export on the page of all highlights: picks a reread-highlights.json file.

reader_marks_copy_hint.message: The .json file is a backup of the highlights and their notes. Import adds the highlights from such a file to the same articles, and to a book imported again from the same .epub file. Nothing already here is changed or removed.
reader_marks_copy_hint.description: Hint under the backup's two buttons. Plain and literal: what the file is, what Import does with it, what it never does.

reader_marks_copy_elsewhere.message: A backup that can be imported (.json) is exported and imported on the page of all highlights.
reader_marks_copy_elsewhere.description: On one document's highlights page, where the backup's buttons do not stand; the link that follows leads to the page of all highlights.

reader_marks_all_link.description: The link after reader_marks_copy_elsewhere: opens the page of all highlights.

reader_marks_export_notes.description: Button under the backup's half, and alone on one document's page: writes reread-highlights.md, the quotes for reading.

reader_marks_notes_hint.message: The .md file is a plain-text list of the quotes and notes, grouped by document - for reading and for your own notes. It cannot be imported.

reader_marks_import_summary_one.description: Plural family over the file's document count; NAME is the picked file's name. The colon leads into the rows below, one per document of the reading list that receives highlights.

reader_marks_import_row_one.description: One row of the import offer: a document of the reading list and how many of the file's highlights it receives.

reader_marks_import_missing_one.message: $COUNT$ document is not in the reading list: $TITLES$. Import it first - a book from its .epub file, an article from the reading list's backup - then import this file again.
reader_marks_import_missing_one.description: Under the offer's rows, only when the file names documents the reading list does not hold. TITLES is a comma-separated sample of their titles.

reader_marks_import_missing_other.message: $COUNT$ documents are not in the reading list: $TITLES$. Import them first - books from their .epub files, articles from the reading list's backup - then import this file again.

reader_marks_import_twins_one.description: In the offer and in the report: the file's highlights that stand here already and are left out.

reader_marks_import_overlap_one.message: $COUNT$ highlight overlaps a highlight already here and is left out.
reader_marks_import_overlap_one.description: In the offer and in the report: a highlight of the file meeting one that stands here is neither merged (that needs the document's text) nor added.

reader_marks_import_overlap_other.message: $COUNT$ highlights overlap highlights already here and are left out.

reader_marks_import_done_one.description: First sentence of the report after the highlights import.

reader_marks_import_nothing.message: There are no highlights to import in that file.
reader_marks_import_nothing.description: The picked file is not a highlights backup, or holds no highlights.

reader_import_marks_elsewhere.message: That is a highlights file. Import it on the Highlights page.
reader_import_marks_elsewhere.description: The reading list's Import was handed reread-highlights.json: that file is read on the Highlights page.

reader_transfer_marks.message: Highlights are included with their articles in the .json backup. The Highlights page exports them on their own: as a .json backup that can be imported - for books too - or as .md notes.

reader_transfer_pick.message: To export only some of the articles, press Select above the list and tick them.
reader_transfer_pick.description: Hint under the Import/Export buttons (D152): the Select button stands above the list, fifty rows up, and a reader about to press Export expects the choice here.

reader_pick_start.description: Button on the reading list's own line over the rows (D152): opens the selection - every article row grows a checkbox, and Export takes the ticked ones.

reader_pick_close.description: Name and tooltip of the cross at the end of the selection's bar: closes the selection and drops the ticks.

reader_pick_all.description: Checkbox over the rows inside the selection: ticks every article the current tab and filter show, on every page; half-ticked while only some of them are.

reader_export_selected.description: The Export button inside the selection: says how many ticked articles the file will hold.

reader_export_done_one.description: Status line after the reading list's export (D153): a download is quiet, so the page says what it wrote - the count, the file's name and its size.

reader_export_marks_done_one.message: Exported the highlights of $COUNT$ document to $FILE$ ($SIZE$).
reader_export_marks_done_one.description: Notice after the highlights page's export (D153): how many documents' quotes the .md holds.

reader_export_marks_done_other.message: Exported the highlights of $COUNT$ documents to $FILE$ ($SIZE$).

vocab_export_done_one.description: Status line after the saved phrases' TSV export (D153).

reader_marks_title.description: The menu row that opens the highlights page (D108), and the page's name before the script says which page it is (the three keys below).

reader_marks_title_all.description: The highlights page's heading when it holds every document's quotes (D152, Michał's call: the heading itself tells the two pages apart).

reader_marks_title_article.description: The heading when the page holds one article's quotes; the article's title stands on the line under it.

reader_marks_title_book.description: The heading when the page holds one book's quotes; the book's title stands on the line under it.

reader_marks_empty.message: Nothing is highlighted yet - highlights are made while reading. Open something from the offline reading list, take the highlighter and mark a passage; it will be waiting here.

reader_marks_empty_doc.message: Nothing is highlighted in this document yet.

reader_marks_back.description: The back arrow's accessible name on an article opened from the highlights page - the step it takes leads there, not to the list.

reader_back_to_doc.description: The back arrow's accessible name on a document's own highlights page - the step back leads to the document itself.

reader_marks_open.description: A quote row's arrow button - it opens the document in the reading view, scrolled to the mark itself.

reader_transfer_link.description: The quiet anchor over the reading list that jumps to the transfer section - it names both kinds of file the section takes, because a book is not obvious from the section's own name.

reader_transfer_accepts.message: Import reads the file it is given: a backup of the re/read article list (.json, or .zip with pictures), or an e-book (.epub).
reader_transfer_accepts.description: The line under the reading list's Import and Export buttons - why there is no separate button for books.

reader_book_label.description: The quiet tag on a book's row in the reading list.

reader_book_part_of.description: A book's place: the segment on screen (or the one reading stopped in) out of how many the book holds.

reader_percent_read.description: The tail of an unread row's detail line, shown once some of the document has been read: how much of the whole has passed before the eyes, in percent.

reader_book_nav.description: Accessible name of the two rows that turn a book's segments.

reader_book_toc.description: The book's table of contents: names the pager button that opens it and titles the dialog itself.

reader_search_title.description: Search inside the open document: names the menu row that opens the dialog and titles the dialog itself.

reader_search_label.description: Invisible label of the search dialog's input, for screen readers.

reader_search_placeholder.description: Placeholder of the search dialog's input.

reader_search_go.description: The button that runs the search over the open document.

reader_search_short.description: Shown instead of results when the query is too short to mean anything.

reader_search_none.description: Shown when the scan finished without a single hit.

reader_search_count_one.description: How many places the phrase was found in. A language may bend the counted noun's case to fit its own sentence.

reader_search_capped.description: Follows the count when the scan stopped at its cap.

reader_library_search_toggle.description: The checkbox under the reading list's filter: with it ticked, the search reads the saved texts themselves, not just titles.

reader_search_more.description: The button that scans the next portion of the list.

reader_search_progress.description: How far the list scan has walked.

reader_search_in_titles.description: Heading over results whose title, site or author carries the phrase.

reader_search_in_text.description: Heading over results whose saved text carries the phrase.

reader_search_more_hits_one.description: The line under a result's snippets when the document holds more hits than the row shows; pressing it opens the document's own search. A language may bend the counted noun's case to fit its own sentence.

close.description: Generic label of a button that puts a dialog away.

reader_book_drm.message: This book is copy-protected (DRM) and cannot be imported.

reader_book_unreadable.message: This file could not be read as an EPUB book.

reader_book_pair_note.message: The book's language is $BOOK$; the current pair translates from $PAIR$.
reader_book_pair_note.description: The quiet line over a book whose language is not the pair's source. Both names come from Intl.DisplayNames in their base form, so the sentence must not bend them grammatically.

reader_import_nothing.message: There are no articles to import in that file.

reader_import_summary_one.description: Plural family over the article count; NAME is the picked file's name. The colon leads into the sample titles shown below.

reader_import_more_one.description: Plural family; the last line of the sample of titles the import confirmation shows, counting the titles it left out.

reader_import_added_one.description: First sentence of the import report, always shown. A language may bend the counted noun's case to fit its own sentence.

reader_import_skipped_other.description: Second sentence of the import report, shown only when something was skipped.

reader_import_unreadable_one.description: Last sentence of the import report, shown only when the file held entries that were not articles.

download_failed.message: The download did not finish, and nothing was stored.

model_download_network.message: Could not reach the place models are kept$DETAIL$. Nothing was stored.
model_download_network.description: DETAIL is a ready-made parenthetical aside like " (timeout)", or empty - the same for every message that carries it.

model_download_http.message: The download was refused$DETAIL$. The model may have moved; nothing was stored.

model_download_size.message: The download ended early$DETAIL$ and was thrown away.

model_download_checksum.message: What arrived is not the model this version expects$DETAIL$, so it was thrown away. Try again - if it keeps happening, the file at the other end has changed.

model_download_unpack.message: The download could not be unpacked$DETAIL$ and was thrown away.

dict_download_network.message: Could not reach the place dictionaries are kept$DETAIL$. Nothing was stored.

dict_download_http.message: The download was refused$DETAIL$. The dictionary may have moved; nothing was stored.

dict_download_too_big.message: The download is far larger than a dictionary should be$DETAIL$, so it was stopped. Nothing was stored.

model_files_unknown_file.message: Not part of a model: $FILE$. Expected names starting with model., lex. and vocab.

model_files_unknown_pair.message: Cannot tell which languages this file is for: $FILE$.

model_files_mixed_pairs.message: Those files are for more than one language pair ($PAIRS$). Load one direction at a time.

model_files_not_a_model.message: Those files are not a translation model.

dict_import_empty.message: No files were selected. Nothing was stored.

dict_import_missing_ifo.message: There is no .ifo file among those, so this is not a StarDict dictionary. Nothing was stored.

dict_import_missing_idx.message: The index is missing (.idx or .idx.gz). Nothing was stored.

dict_import_missing_dict.message: The dictionary body is missing (.dict or .dict.dz). Nothing was stored.

dict_import_mixed.message: Those files belong to more than one dictionary ($NAMES$). Add one at a time. Nothing was stored.

dict_import_not_stardict.message: That .ifo file is not a StarDict dictionary. Nothing was stored.

dict_import_not_stardict_detail.message: That is $KIND$, which this extension cannot read. Nothing was stored.

dict_import_unpack.message: The files are compressed in a way that could not be unpacked$DETAIL$. Nothing was stored.

dict_import_no_entries.message: The index is empty - there are no words in this dictionary. Nothing was stored.

dict_import_no_entries_detail.message: Not one of the $COUNT$ words in the index could be read, so the files do not belong together. Nothing was stored.

dict_import_unreadable.message: Those files are not a dictionary this extension can read. Nothing was stored.

zip_not_zip.message: What arrived is not a zip archive. Nothing was stored.

zip_unsupported.message: The archive uses a feature this extension does not read$DETAIL$. Nothing was stored.

zip_too_big.message: The archive is larger than a dictionary has any reason to be$DETAIL$. Nothing was stored.

zip_bad.message: The archive is damaged$DETAIL$. Nothing was stored - try downloading again.

zip_unreadable.message: The archive could not be read. Nothing was stored.

words_one.description: Plural family: the _one/_few/_many/_other suffixes follow Intl.PluralRules categories; a missing category falls back to _other.

options_local_intro.message: Everything re/read does happens on this device (offline): translating, the dictionary, the reading list, your saved phrases. Nothing you read or select is ever sent anywhere. An internet connection is needed only when you want to download a new translation model or a dictionary - and only from the two URLs shown openly in those sections.

options_first_steps_intro.message: Nothing translates yet - the model that would do it is not yet on this device. Setting up takes a minute:
options_first_steps_intro.description: Opens the first-steps block, shown on the settings page only while no model is stored.

options_first_steps_model.message: Under "Translation models", find the language pair you need (the filter finds it fastest) and press "Download". The model is stored on this device and translates offline from then on - and the first model sets the language pair above by itself.
options_first_steps_model.description: Quotes the options_models_heading section name and the action_download button - each language quotes its own wording of those keys, so the three must move together.

options_first_steps_dictionary.message: Under "Dictionaries", download a dictionary for the same pair (optional, but worth it) - single words then get fuller answers than a translation alone (after pressing "More" in the translation bubble).
options_first_steps_dictionary.description: Quotes the options_dictionaries_heading section name and the bubble_more button - each language quotes its own wording of those keys, so they must move together.

options_first_steps_pin.message: Last, pin re/read to the toolbar: the puzzle-piece icon at the right end of the bar, then the gear next to re/read and "Pin to Toolbar". The button opens the reader, the reading list, your saved phrases and the switch for the site you are on.
options_first_steps_pin.description: The desktop wording of the last step; on Android the page swaps in options_first_steps_pin_android instead. Quotes Firefox's own "Pin to Toolbar" menu label - each language must quote Firefox's official wording of it, not a translation of its own.

options_first_steps_pin_android.message: The re/read button is in the browser menu (⋮), under Extensions - it opens the reader, the reading list, your saved phrases and the switch for the site you are on.
options_first_steps_pin_android.description: Replaces options_first_steps_pin on Android, where there is no toolbar to pin anything to - the button already sits in the browser menu.

options_sections_aria.description: Accessible name of the row of anchor links under the intro.

options_engine_value.message: Bergamot, inside the package - translates offline

options_storage_value.message: $SIZE$ - the models, the dictionaries, the reading list and your phrases together
options_storage_value.description: The size line of the storage row. $SIZE$ is the amount, already formatted with its unit.

options_storage_how.message: Disk space used by the extension. Dictionaries take up more space than their file size because of the database structure. Deleting an article or book completely removes its text, images, highlights, notes and reading progress.

options_storage_persistent.message: Persistent storage: granted. The browser has promised not to clear this data to make room.

options_storage_at_risk.message: Persistent storage: not granted. Safari clears a site's data after about a month of use without a tap on its pages, and this extension's pages count as one site. Your phrases have a copy that survives this (the line below); the models, the dictionaries and the reading list do not - open the reader or these settings now and then.
options_storage_at_risk.description: Shown only in WebKit browsers, where a refused persistence means the browser may delete the extension's data by itself. The line below is options_storage_backup.

options_storage_backup_one.message: Copy of the vocabulary: $COUNT$ phrase, written $WHEN$ - kept where the browser does not clear data on its own.
options_storage_backup_one.description: Plural family over the phrase count; $WHEN$ is a date and time in the reader's own calendar.

options_storage_backup_other.message: Copy of the vocabulary: $COUNT$ phrases, written $WHEN$ - kept where the browser does not clear data on its own.

options_storage_backup_none.message: Copy of the vocabulary: none yet - it is written with the next phrase you save.

options_storage_marks_backup_one.message: Copy of the highlights: $COUNT$ highlight with its notes, written $WHEN$.
options_storage_marks_backup_one.description: Plural family over the highlight count; $WHEN$ is a date and time in the reader's own calendar.

options_storage_marks_backup_other.message: Copy of the highlights: $COUNT$ highlights with their notes, written $WHEN$.

options_storage_marks_backup_none.message: Copy of the highlights: none yet - it is written with the next highlight you make.

options_storage_library_copy_one.message: Copy of the reading list: $COUNT$ document, $SIZE$.
options_storage_library_copy_one.description: Plural family over the document count; $SIZE$ is a size such as "12.4 MB".

options_storage_library_copy_other.message: Copy of the reading list: $COUNT$ documents, $SIZE$.

options_storage_library_copy_none.message: Copy of the reading list: none yet - it is written with the next page you save or book you import.

options_storage_library_copy_off.message: Copy of the reading list: off.

options_library_copy_hint.message: Creates a backup of your reading list to protect it against automatic browser cleanups and database errors. This doubles the disk space the list takes, but keeps your saved articles safe if the database is lost.

reader_marks_delete_all_one.message: Delete the $COUNT$ quote of this page
reader_marks_delete_all_one.description: Plural family; the quiet text act under the missing-document note on the highlights page (D150), naming how many quotes the document-wide deletion takes. Shown only for more than one quote - the one-form is the family's formality.

reader_marks_delete_all_other.message: Delete all $COUNT$ quotes of this page

reader_mark_text_changed.message: The page's text has changed since this was highlighted, so the highlight cannot be shown here.
reader_mark_text_changed.description: The notice under the bar when the highlights page's arrow lands on a mark the quote guard refused to paint: the saved page no longer reads the quote at its anchor (D151).

reader_marks_missing_doc.message: Its document is no longer saved - this quote came back from the copy. Open the page again and the highlight will be there.
reader_marks_missing_doc.description: Under a quote on the highlights page whose document is gone from the reading list; the quote was restored from the copy kept in storage.local.

options_pair_hint.message: Shows the language pairs downloaded to this device. To add new languages, download them in the
options_pair_hint.description: Followed by an anchor link wearing the options_models_heading text, then options_pair_hint_rest. No part starts or ends with whitespace.

options_pair_hint_rest.description: The end of the pair hint, after the anchor link that wears the options_models_heading text; closes the sentence with its own full stop. Must not start or end with whitespace.

options_pair_none.message: No model or dictionary yet - add one below
options_pair_none.description: The only line of the pair select, disabled, while neither a model nor a dictionary is stored on the device.

options_pair_dictionary_only.description: A pair-select line whose pair only an installed dictionary vouches for - no model on the device serves it.

options_pair_hint_quiet.message: Without a translation model, the pair says which language you are reading and where saved phrases are kept. Pairs come from installed models and dictionaries.
options_pair_hint_quiet.description: The pair row's hint while translation is switched off, replacing options_pair_hint.

options_reading_pair_quiet.message: Reading $FROM$ - machine translation is off, and saved phrases are kept under this pair.
options_reading_pair_quiet.description: Status line after choosing a pair while translation is switched off.

options_reader_only_hint.message: Limits the underlining of saved phrases and the translation bubble to the reader. Selecting text on an ordinary web page will only show an option to open the page in the reader. On Android and iOS it is on by default.

options_keep_articles.message: Save in the offline reading list by default

options_keep_articles_hint.message: Automatically saves every page you open in the reader for offline reading. Your saved pages, highlights and reading progress are kept safe even if the original website changes or disappears.

options_font_custom_hint.message: Type the name of a font installed on this device, for example Georgia or Noto Serif. The reading view's Type row will then offer it as Custom. Leave the field empty to use the built-in typefaces only.

options_quiet_bubble_hint.message: Shows only the translated text in the bubble. The action buttons (such as copy or save) appear only when you click or tap the bubble.

options_no_translation_hint.message: Turns off machine translation (the model). The reader, the offline reading list and the highlighter keep working. With a language pair chosen, the bubble still shows dictionary meanings, and you can save phrases and see their underlines. Ideal for reading with dictionaries or in your native language. Your saved data is not deleted and returns when you turn this off.

options_bubble_off_hint.message: With this on, selecting text on an ordinary page does nothing at all - open a page in the reader from re/read's button or with Alt+Shift+R. In the reader a selection is only a highlight for the moment: no bubble opens, a tap or Escape clears it, and Ctrl+C or Cmd+C copies it (on a touch screen nothing can be copied).
options_bubble_off_hint.description: Under the sub-option of the translation-off switch on the settings page (D149); the row shows only while that switch is on. Alt+Shift+R is the extension's keyboard shortcut for opening the reader.

options_bubble_scale_hint.message: Adjusts the text and button size inside the translation bubble across all pages.

options_note_more.description: The accessible name of the chevron that opens a folded description on the settings page (D155); `aria-expanded` carries the state.

options_tts_hint.message: Enables the text-to-speech function. Turning this off hides all read-aloud buttons in the bubble, lists, and the reader.
options_tts_hint.description: Under the reading-aloud switch on the settings page (D148). Off, the voice and speed rows below it hide as well.

options_tts_lang.description: The accessible name of the language select in the voice row of the settings page (D155): which language the voice beside it is chosen for. The options are language names, so the select carries no visible label of its own.

options_tts_voice_hint.message: Select the voice used to read phrases and articles in each language. Only voices that speak offline are offered: speech is made on this device and nothing is sent to the internet.
options_tts_voice_hint.description: Under the voice select on the settings page. True by construction (D155): `voicesFor` in lib/tts.js keeps out every voice the engine marks as remote (localService false), and nothing speaks through one.

speech_no_offline_voice.message: This device has no offline voice for this language.
speech_no_offline_voice.description: Where a speaker was refused for want of an offline voice (D155): the device lists voices, and none of them reads the language without the network. Under the voice select on the settings page, in the reader's notice line, in the saved phrases page's status line.

options_models_intro.message: Download a translation model here for each language pair you want to translate. These are official Mozilla files that run entirely offline on your device.

options_update_list.description: The button that fetches today's list of models - the one network request no download makes.

options_list_dated.description: Beside the update button of both catalogues; the date stands after this as its own emphasized element. Must not start or end with whitespace.

options_filter_models_label.message: Filter the list of translation models

options_show_all.description: Unfolds a catalogue past its installed rows; the count is the whole list.

options_model_note_from.description: First half of the note around the host, which stands between the parts as a page element. Each part must read on from the last across a plain space - no part starts or ends with whitespace.

options_model_note_rest.message: - where Mozilla publishes them. The extension connects to this public server only when you press Update the list or Download. No personal data is ever sent.

options_add_model_summary.message: To add by hand a model the list above does not offer, load its files here.
options_add_model_summary.description: The one visible line of the folded-by-hand section - says when opening it is worth it.

options_add_model_intro.message: Pick the three files of one direction and they are stored locally. Gzipped files are unpacked here, so the downloads can be used as they come:

options_files_note.message: Adding a model by hand makes no network request, and this page stays the way in on the day the place models are downloaded from stops answering.

options_dictionaries_intro.message: Add dictionaries to see detailed word definitions in the translation bubble. You can change the order in which they appear using the arrows.

options_dictionary_order_hint.message: The bubble answers in the order below. Only the dictionaries of the language you are reading answer.
options_dictionary_order_hint.description: Above the list of dictionaries, shown only once a second one is stored.

options_dictionary_note_from.description: First half of the note around the host, which stands between the parts as a page element. Each part must read on from the last across a plain space - no part starts or ends with whitespace.

options_dictionary_note_rest.message: - where WikDict publishes the dictionaries it builds from Wiktionary (CC BY-SA). The extension connects to this public server only when you press Update the list or Download. No personal data is ever sent.

options_add_dictionary_summary.message: Import your own dictionaries in the StarDict format. Unpack the archive, select the required files (.ifo, .idx, .dict), choose the languages and press Add dictionary.
options_add_dictionary_summary.description: The whole instruction of the fold that adds a dictionary from files; the list of file kinds stands under it.

options_file_syn.message: - other spellings, when the dictionary has them

options_add_dictionary_mono.message: A monolingual dictionary works too, for example English-English: choose the same language on both sides.

options_dict_files_note.message: Adding from files makes no network request. Any StarDict files work, including the catalogue's own, which are published at
options_dict_files_note.description: Ends just before the address, which stands in the page as a link; the sentence's closing full stop is part of the page.

options_disabled_intro.message: A list of websites where the extension is switched off (no translation or underlines). You can add sites here using the extension icon in your browser's toolbar.

options_support_intro.message: re/read is built by a non-profit foundation - no investors, no ads, no tracking. If you find it useful and want to support its continued development, every donation helps us build software free from commercial pressure.

options_delete_confirm.description: The armed Delete of a model or dictionary row, asking in place; the second press deletes.

options_delete_model_aria.description: Accessible name of a model row's Delete at rest - a bare "Delete" in a list names nothing.

options_delete_confirm_aria.description: The same button, armed and asking; shared by models (the pair label) and dictionaries (the name).

options_about_dictionary.description: Summary of the fold holding a stored dictionary's publisher, licence and description.

options_checking_model.message: Checking the $PAIR$ model in the engine...
options_checking_model.description: Shown while a fresh copy of the translation engine trial-loads the downloaded or hand-picked files, before anything is stored.

options_model_rejected.message: The engine could not load what arrived$DETAIL$. Nothing was stored.

options_refresh_failed.message: Could not refresh the list$DETAIL$. The list from $DATE$ stays.

options_version_unknown.description: Beside an installed model that never recorded which published version it came from - added from files, or stored before sources were recorded. The update check makes no claim about it.

options_downloaded_model.message: Downloaded the $PAIR$ model, $SIZE$ on this device.

options_store_failed.message: The model downloaded but could not be stored: $DETAIL$

options_reading_pair_missing.message: Reading $FROM$, translating into $TO$ - and there is no model for this direction here yet.

options_no_models.message: No models here, and none to download - this build lists none.

options_filter_no_match_models.message: No pair matches that. The filter takes a language name or a code.

options_filter_no_match_dictionaries.message: No dictionary matches that. The filter takes a language name or a code.

options_no_disabled.message: No sites are switched off. The toolbar popup is where one is.

options_added_model.message: Added the $PAIR$ model, $SIZE$ on this device.

options_deleting_dictionary.message: Deleting $NAME$ - a large dictionary takes a while...
options_deleting_dictionary.description: The dictionary section's status line from the moment Delete is confirmed until the database lets the rows go - tens of seconds for a million rows on a tablet.

options_deleting_row.description: The meta cell of the row being deleted, in place of its counts; its buttons are gone.

options_move_dictionary_up_aria.description: Accessible name of the up arrow on a stored dictionary's row; the arrow itself is the visible label.

options_dictionary_moved.description: Said after an arrow moves a dictionary; the row that moved may be out of sight, and a screen reader has nothing else to go on.

options_no_catalog.message: No dictionaries to download - this build lists none.

options_skipped_entries_one.message: $COUNT$ entry could not be read and was left out.

options_skipped_entries_other.message: $COUNT$ entries could not be read and were left out.

options_swept_unfinished.message: Removed a dictionary that was never finished importing ($NAMES$).

options_import_interrupted.message: Interrupted at $DONE$ of $TOTAL$ - Continue picks up from there.
options_import_interrupted.description: The meta cell of a stored dictionary whose import stopped halfway (a killed tab); DONE and TOTAL are records, bare numbers. Quotes the options_continue_import button, so the two move together.

options_import_interrupted_early.message: Interrupted before the first entry was stored - Continue starts it over.
options_import_interrupted_early.description: The same row when the import died before its first batch landed. Quotes options_continue_import.

options_import_elsewhere.message: Another tab is adding a dictionary right now - wait for it to finish.
options_import_elsewhere.description: Both the meta cell of an unfinished row while another tab holds the import lock, and the status line when Add or Continue is pressed meanwhile.

options_continue_import.description: The button on an unfinished dictionary's row that picks its import up where it stopped. Quoted by options_import_interrupted and options_import_interrupted_early.
